1.note: Literally "which everyone who comes upon it, and stands". Read as: a saying that makes the hearer stop and take it in. The sense is uncertain.

2.note: A play on two verbs that differ in one letter: יֵקַל "is made light (of no worth)" and יֵקַר "is precious (honored)".

3.note: The edition runs the end of one saying and the start of the next into one line; the English keeps that line as it is.

4.note: The edition marks a gap here, so words are missing. יְקַר רוּחַ is from Prov 17:27 ("cool of spirit", or "precious of spirit"). Perhaps the lost words said that calm reserve which is not from humility looks like pride.

5.note: עִיִּים are heaps of ruins (Mic 1:6, Ps 79:1): youth wore itself out among the wrecks of lust.

6.note: The verb is read as "be dispossessed, become poor", as in Prov 20:13 and 23:21, against "grows rich" in the next line.

7.note: Literally "his enemy will return him" (or "answer him"). Read as: he who cannot forgive a friend will get his due from enemies. The sense is uncertain.

8.note: A sound play: תְּשׁוּבָה "repentance, return" from מְשׁוּבָה "backsliding" (Jer 3:22, Hos 14:5). The pairs also rhyme: נְקִיוּת / אַכְזָרִיּוּת, טָהֳרָה / עֲבֵרָה.

9.note: Literally "and wise men you have made foolish" (the verb as in Isa 44:25 and 2 Sam 15:31): the students have outdone the wise. Praise, not blame.

10.note: "The Precious One" may be God, who calls by name (Isa 43:1, 45:3), or "the honored one"; perhaps also "honor itself named me". The sense is uncertain.

11.he: אֵלוֹן בְּצַעְנַנִּים מְגוּרוֹתַי / אוּלָם שְׁמִי חֶבֶר יְלִיד קֵינִי
11.note: In Judg 4:11, Ḥever the Kenite pitched his tent at Elon-bezaanannim (the written form בצעננים). The hero names himself through the biblical Ḥever's dwelling. So the old man is Ḥever.

12.note: תְּעוּדָה is "testimony" and also "teaching" (Isa 8:16, 8:20). Read as "the crown of all teaching".
